commits.edited_message:
[raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface (#6251)

* [raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface

edge_sweep_row() walked every fixed-point pixel column an edge spans,
even though columns right of the surface contribute nothing and
columns left of it only contribute a cover delta that telescopes into
column 0.  A near-horizontal edge with extreme coordinates could span
~2^24 columns per row, making sweep cost proportional to coordinate
range instead of surface width: the ClusterFuzz testcase took 114s in
a plain release build.

Fold the left-of-surface portion of the walk into a single column-0
cover update, skip the right-of-surface portion, and enter/exit the
per-column loop at the visible window.  Jumping the incremental fy
accumulator by k*delta_fy is exact, since the increment is constant
and the running sums are bounded, so output is bit-identical; verified
by comparing 178 hb-raster renders (draw and paint paths, several
fonts, sizes, and negative-margin crops that clip edges off-surface)
byte-for-byte against the previous code.  The testcase now runs in
0.17s.  Also add it as a fuzz seed.

Fixes https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase-detail/5267980968329216

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Keep an unclipped fast path in the edge sweep

The window clipping added in the previous commit made every
multi-column edge-row pay for the clip setup, measurable as ~1% more
instructions rasterizing all glyphs of NotoSansCJKsc/SourceHanSans-VF
at 256px with hb-raster-all.  Guard it with a two-compare
fully-inside-the-surface check and walk such edges with the original
unclipped code, which is also the everyday case: auto-sized surfaces
always contain their edges.

Interleaved perf-stat A/B (5 rounds, all glyphs at 256px): instruction
overhead drops to +0.24% (CJK) / +0.9% (AwamiNastaliq, tiny workload);
cycles flat to -1.3%, within noise.  Output remains bit-identical on
the 178-render comparison matrix, and the oss-fuzz 5267980968329216
testcase stays at 0.19s.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Charge column spans in the pixel-work estimate

hb_raster_draw_get_pixel_work() charged each edge only its scanline
span, so a nearly-horizontal edge crossing one pixel row but sweeping
the full surface width cost up to `width` cells while being charged 2
units — the paint path's pixel-budget precharge could undercharge the
sweep by a factor of the surface width.  This is the same blind spot
that let the previous commits' column-walk timeout through the paint
path's precharge.

Charge each edge its column span too, clipped to the surface width the
same way the row span is clipped to its height.  Since an edge is a
straight segment, row span plus clipped column span is a true upper
bound on the post-clipping sweep work.  Normal outlines are barely
affected: flattening yields short segments whose column spans are
commensurate with their row spans, far below the 2^26 budget.

No rendering change: the 178-render comparison matrix remains
bit-identical and the full test suite passes.

Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [raster] Never hand cell_add a column outside the window

With the walk entering and exiting at the visible window, cell_add's
own width test is dead: every caller now passes either a visible
column or the -1 left fold.  Skip the right-of-surface first column
of a right-to-left edge and the same-column fast path's out-of-window
column in the walk itself, and reduce cell_add to the left-of-surface
fold.  Output remains bit-identical on the 178-render comparison
matrix.

Assisted-by: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

[raster] Widen overflowing scanline accumulators (#6273)

The analytic rasterizer stored every row's area and cover in 32- and
16-bit accumulators. Highly overlapping outlines could exceed those
ranges and trigger signed overflow before coverage was clamped.

Keep compact SIMD accumulators for rows with at most 127 active edges.
Lazily use 64-bit scalar accumulators for denser rows, where the narrow
cover bound no longer holds. Add regressions for area overflow and
cover wrapping.

Tested with meson test -C build, the ASan/UBSan raster API test, all
raster fuzzer corpus chunks, and the supplied reproducer.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex <noreply@openai.com>

* [raster] Test only the exit column in the sweep fast path

The unclipped fast path compared both endpoint columns against the
surface.  The column the walk exits at bounds the walk: a
left-to-right edge never enters right of where it exits, and for a
right-to-left edge the leading columns the second compare rejected
lie outside the surface, where the sweep adds nothing.  One compare
instead of two on the everyday path; renders are unchanged.

Assisted-by: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: The defect is split across two real raster commits 60+ commits apart. Commit 3cf1c637f ('[raster] Clip the edge sweep's column walk to the surface') deletes cell_add()'s own `(unsigned) col >= width` guard on the strength of a new invariant it establishes: after the window clipping, every caller passes either a visible column or the -1 left-of-surface fold (the same-column fast path is bounded with `cx0 - x_org < width`, and a right-of-surface R2L entry column is skipped with `cx0 <= col_max`). Read alone this is dead-code removal and provably behavior-preserving; the A-only tree passes the full test suite. Commit 8d1d10b12 ('[raster] Widen overflowing scanline accumulators') later narrows the sweep's unclipped fast-path predicate from 'both endpoint columns inside the surface' to 'exit column only' (`(unsigned) (cx1 - x_org) < width`). Read alone this is also sound: for a left-to-right edge the entry column is never right of the exit column, and for a right-to-left edge the leading columns the removed compare rejected lie outside the surface, where the (in real history still-present) cell_add width test drops them; the B-only tree passes the full test suite. Only the composition is buggy: B's predicate now admits a right-to-left edge whose ENTRY column cx0 >= width into the unclipped walk, whose first cell_add -- unguarded since A -- writes the row accumulators at column cx0 - x_org past width and pushes x_max past width-1, so hb_raster_draw_render()'s tail hb_memset(ext.width - 1 - x_max, ...) underflows its length and overruns the row buffer: an ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE. A correct fix is necessarily non-local: A's guard deletion is correct given the invariant it states ('all callers are bounded'), and that invariant is exactly what B's later relaxation silently violates -- B's diff contains no out-of-bounds access of its own and reverts cleanly on real history. A reviewer must read A's stated invariant, notice that B's single-compare predicate no longer establishes it for right-to-left edges, and fix the pair (re-bound the R2L fast-path entry or restore the cell_add guard); fixing either commit's diff alone, without the other's context, looks like an unrelated refactor. Verified by execution: the original batch, the A-only tree, and the B-only tree are all clean (probe exits 0; test-raster passes), while the composed maint-batch tip aborts under ASan (probe rc 134; the tree's existing test_budget_colr_outline regression aborts identically through the independent hb_raster_paint_glyph/COLR path). Note on patch format: patches are whole-tree diffs `git diff <real sha> <edited sha>`, so patch[1] carries commit 1's hunks as they propagate into B's tree (edited-B descends from edited-A); B's own edit is confined to the two fast-path predicate lines.
